Amandeep: I keep saying flat, flat, flat. You keep saying trip. That's the fourth time we've had this fight.
Bhupen: Because a life without trips isn't one I want to save for.
Amandeep: And to me the flat is the reason we work.
Bhupen: What if we stop arguing about who's right and ask what each thing is for? For me a trip is feeling free.
Amandeep: And the flat is feeling safe.
Bhupen: Then what if sixty percent of what we set aside goes to the flat, and forty to travel?
Amandeep: Sixty and forty. Can we look at it again in a year?
Bhupen: Deal. One good trip a year is still real.
Amandeep: And I don't feel I've lost the flat.

qa.q: What split did Amandeep and Bhupen agree on?
qa.a: They agreed on sixty percent to the flat and forty to travel.

qa.q: What does the flat mean to Amandeep, and how does Amandeep feel about it?
qa.a: The flat means feeling safe to Amandeep, and Amandeep is relieved that it has not been given up.

qa.q: What else could the couple do to keep the agreement working, and why?
qa.a: They could review it after a year as agreed and note what each goal has given them, because priorities may shift.

qa.q: How might Bhupen have felt when the trip was kept in the plan?
qa.a: Bhupen was probably relieved and appreciated, since travel stayed a real part of the plan and not a dismissed wish.

grounding: Illustrates a couple with different money priorities agreeing a percentage for each goal after asking what saving and travel mean to each, so neither feels dismissed.

subtype: Approach: values-first planning about saving versus spending [Thinking]
passage:
The fight wasn't really about the Goa trip. It was about what each of us thought money was for.
Revathi wanted to save every spare rupee for a flat. Her parents had rented all their lives and moved seven times. For me, travel was the thing. I grew up in one small town and only saw the sea at twenty-two.
Bhupen, my oldest friend, listened to both of us one evening and asked a simple question: "Why does each of you want this?"
That changed the conversation. Revathi talked about the seven moves. I talked about the sea. We stopped thinking the other person was being foolish.
Then we agreed a split: most of what we save each month goes to the flat fund, and a fixed smaller percentage goes to a travel fund. Both goals move, just at different speeds.
Revathi booked Goa for next March. I checked the flat fund.
— Pranav

qa.q: How many times had Revathi's parents moved?
How did Pranav and Revathi feel about each other's priorities once they explained their reasons?
qa.a: They felt understood and less dismissive, no longer seeing the other person's goal as foolish.

qa.q: What else could Pranav and Revathi do to make the split last?
qa.a: They could look at the percentages together every few months and, if unsure about the flat plans, talk to a qualified adviser about their options.

qa.q: How might Bhupen see the change in the couple after that question?
qa.a: Bhupen may feel glad and relieved, seeing his friends move from arguing to planning together.

grounding: It shows a couple where one wants to save for a flat and the other values travel, agreeing a percentage for each goal so neither priority is dismissed.

Facilitator's note — Saturday couples' workshop on shared planning, community hall, Vadodara. Written by Deepika.

Himani and Varun came to the third session visibly tense. Varun explained that he wanted to save every month towards a flat. Himani said she loved travelling and felt he saw it as a waste.
I asked each of them to write, privately, why their goal mattered. Varun wrote that his family had lost a rented home when he was ten. Himani wrote that travel was the only time she felt fully herself.
When they read each other's notes, both went quiet. Varun said, "I didn't know that's what it meant to you."
Before leaving, they agreed on their own plan: a larger percentage each month for the flat, a smaller fixed percentage for travel. Himani smiled for the first time that day.
What I did next: I noted to check in with them at the final session.

qa.q: Where was the couples' workshop held?
qa.a: At the community hall in Vadodara.

qa.q: How did Himani feel before and after the percentage plan?
qa.a: Himani felt tense and dismissed at first, as if travel was seen as waste, then happier once both goals had a share, smiling for the first time that day.

qa.q: What else could Himani and Varun do to keep the plan working?
qa.a: They could review the percentages together each year, and if they want help with the flat, speak with a qualified adviser.

qa.q: How might Varun see the agreement after reading Himani's note?
qa.a: Varun understands why travel matters to her, so he may feel less anxious about the flat goal being threatened and more at ease with sharing.

grounding: It shows a couple where one wants to save for a flat and the other values travel agreeing a percentage for each, so neither priority is dismissed.
